On Thursday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said an “unknown projectile” had struck a tanker in Hormuz this week, causing a fire that was later extinguished.

articles.title: Race to get aid into Nepal and Tibet amid warnings flood lake could burst
articles.summary: Flash floods have killed at least 469 people while homes and infrastructure have been swept away
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu, Sam Jones and Amy Hawkins

blocks.text: The international community was scrambling to get aid into flood-stricken parts of Nepal and Tibet on Thursday as authorities warned that a lake ⁠formed at the ⁠site ⁠where the ​deadly torrents occurred ⁠was rising and ⁠at risk ​of ‌bursting.
The catastrophic flash floods that hit Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, thundering down valleys and obliterating entire villages, killed at least 469 people and left more than 1,300 missing.

Efforts to locate those unaccounted for – including hundreds of tourists from India, the US, Britain, Australia and Canada – have been complicated by the destruction of dozens of bridges and 25 miles (40km) of roads in the mountainous region, which is popular with trekkers and pilgrims.
Nepali army helicopter rescue teams were working on Friday to rescue about 100 people trapped inside a tunnel at a hydropower project swamped by the devastating flood.
“Our focus is in search and rescue of people … some people are trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project,” said Nepal army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet.

“Two helicopters have been dispatched but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel. Relief efforts are also under way to provide the rescued people what they need.”
The prime minister’s office said the army was working in tough conditions and had already rescued 350 workers and local people who were trapped in the tunnel amid the risky conditions.

Rescue teams reported finding bodies hundreds of miles downstream from the disaster zone in the Chitwan district of Nepal, near the border with India. Dozens of injured people were transported to Kathmandu for advanced medical care and more than 100 people were rescued by Nepali army personnel in helicopters.
Videos from Wednesday showed a massive wall of water crashing down on the border as people tried to flee. The power, volume and speed of the floods gave little time for escape.
Trucks were overturned and houses, roads ⁠and power plants were swept away in Nepal, while ​officials in Tibet said they feared “major casualties” after a mudslide hit a border crossing.

Tom Fletcher, the UN’s humanitarian chief, described the flood as “horrifying”. He said emergency teams had been mobilised and an initial $2m (£1.5m) of disaster funds allocated to cover emergency medical care, shelter and water.

Nepal’s disaster authority warned of continuing danger on Thursday, appealing to residents and rescuers to stay away from a swelling lake that had formed at the flood site. Chinese authorities said a barrier lake at the confluence of the Tsogyal and Purupqiangzangbu rivers was overflowing and could burst.
Girilal Budhathoki, 36, who lives in the Rasuwa district of Nepal’s Bagmati province, said the flood waters swept away his wife and four children while he was away from the family home.
“A huge surge of water came,” he said. “Everything turned completely black, and I couldn’t understand what was happening. Suddenly, something heavy crushed me and I fell down.”

Budhathoki realised what had happened only when he returned to the place where his house had stood. “I searched desperately for my wife and children but I couldn’t find them,” he said. “They didn’t make it out. My wife was swept away too. I am all alone now.”

Kamal Kharel, who works at a hydropower plant in Chilime, also in Rasuwa district, was in the office when the floods hit. “The whole place shook as if there had been a huge earthquake,” he said. “But when I went outside, I saw everything a storm and raging water.”

Kharel and some of his colleagues managed to climb a hill, where they stayed until they were rescued by the army on Thursday morning. “I had never seen waves crashing that high. You only see waves like that in the sea.”

People from the hard-hit districts of Nuwakot and Dhading, in Bagmati province, were seen gathering outside an army training centre – the base for helicopter rescue operations – seeking information about missing family members.

Police were recording the names of the missing outside the barracks gate. Mobile phone torches were their only source of light as the area remained without electricity because of damaged hydroelectric infrastructure.

blocks.caption: Flooding has caused widespread damage to homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure in Nuwakot, Nepal.   Photograph: Ap Tolang/Nexpher/Zuma Press/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The village of Soley, in Nuwakot, which had about 25 homes, was almost wiped out, according to Nirajan Paudyal, a Kathmandu-based journalist whose parents and other relatives lived there. Desperate for information, he had travelled to the area on Thursday for news of his family. “There is no update till now,” he said. “I fear there won’t be any update.”

More than 500 foreigners were among 826 people missing in Nepal, police and tourism ⁠officials said. Among those unaccounted for were 177 from India, 90 from the US, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada.
Chinese state media said at least 558 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, of whom at least 260 were foreign nationals.
Many of the victims were on a pilgrimage to Kailash Mansarovar, a high-altitude site in ‌Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists among others.

Early reports from Nepali ​officials suggested an earthquake could have caused the lower part of a glacier to collapse and trigger ‌the floods. But the US Geological Survey later said what was initially reported ‌as a 4.4-magnitude earthquake was a seismic shock generated by glacial rock and ice collapsing, causing the flood of debris. “No earthquake had occurred,” it said.

Srijana Gurung, the acting Nepal director for the international NGO Plan International, said communities across the Himalayan country were facing “climate shock after shock” with hardly any time to recover.

“Floods and landslides have always happened in Nepal but the climate crisis is making them far more frequent and intense,” she said. “The priority now must be reaching those affected, supporting families searching for loved ones and ensuring vulnerable communities have the assistance they need.”

Gurung said children and families who had lost their homes and livelihoods would be in urgent need of medical help, food, shelter and hygiene kits. “There is also a risk of waterborne disease as access to clean water and sanitation is likely to have been damaged,” she said.

blocks.caption: People look at the devastation left by flash flooding in Nepal’s Nuwakot district.  Photograph: Rajesh Kumar Singh/AP

blocks.text: Scant information emerged from Chinese authorities about the scale of the destruction. Tibet is the most tightly controlled part of China even under normal circumstances. Foreign journalists cannot visit the region unless they are part of a government-controlled tour and the authorities have cracked down harshly on calls for greater autonomy from the Tibetan people. Tibetans have almost no contact with the international media because of fears of retribution.

Only brief, state-controlled media reports about the floods have been allowed to circulate in China and the authorities have confirmed only three deaths. Chinese reports have focused on rescue efforts.

Maya Wang, the deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch, wrote on X: “The floods raise questions about whether Chinese authorities could’ve done more to reduce disaster risks, given longstanding concerns from Tibetan diaspora groups and experts about rapid, state-led development in areas where Tibetans have little say.”
She called on Beijing to “allow Tibetans access to information and international researchers and journalists unfettered access to the region, and conduct a rigorous investigation into the disaster”.

articles.title: Bondi library returns book How to Sell a Genocide to shelves after State Library ‘outlines the law’
articles.summary: Book was removed for review earlier this month following complaint but reinstated after petition and State Library letter to Waverley council

blocks.text: A Sydney library has returned to its borrowing shelves a book critical of Israel called How to Sell a Genocide following a public campaign and an intervention from the State Library of New South Wales.
Waverley library removed the book “for review” earlier this month after the Jewish news outlet JWire reported it had approached the council.

JWire said a survivor of December’s antisemitic attack at Bondi, during which 15 people were killed, saw How to Sell a Genocide on the “new release / hot item” shelf and wrote on Facebook that the display was distressing for survivors and bereaved families.
Guardian Australia was unable to locate the Facebook post. Waverley library at Bondi Junction is in the same council area as Bondi beach.
A staff member at the council-operated library on Friday confirmed the book was back on its shelves. Waverley council was contacted for comment.

The State Library had written to the council reminding it of its obligations under guidelines issued by the Library Council of NSW and the Library Act “which was amended in 2026 to reinforce their independence to develop and maintain collections”.
“The State Library of NSW supports free and equitable access to information,” a spokesperson said.

“The library acknowledges that some books and materials may not align with everyone’s personal views, experiences or beliefs, but supports the right of individuals to make their own choices about what they read, view and access.
“The library has outlined to Waverley council the law and policy relevant to this situation.”

Ramia Abdo Sultan, a lawyer, helped organise a change.org petition calling for the book to be returned to the shelves. She said in a social media post on Thursday that Waverley library’s manager had notified staff that was happening.
“There are 21 people so far queued up in a waiting list for that book,” Abdo Sultan, a board member of the Australia Palestine Advocacy Network, said.
The petition to restore the book was signed by almost 2,500 people.
“We acknowledge and respect the grief and trauma experienced by victims of violence and antisemitism,” it stated.

“However, individual distress, offence or political disagreement should not determine what the broader public is permitted to access through a public library. Readers should be afforded the opportunity to access books freely and form their own opinions on the contents of the book.”
The book, published by Pluto Press and written by Adam Johnson, critiques what it claims is the US media’s “complicity in the destruction of Gaza”.

Johnson welcomed the decision to reinstate his book but criticised the council for “thus far refusing to answer what complaint prompted the book’s removal”. Johnson said he hoped to find out “through legal channels”.
“It’s obviously a good development the council decided to end their ban of the book amid pressure from free speech and Palestine activists, whose support I am grateful for,” he said.
after newsletter promotion

“But it was never about one library or one book, but about the increased suppression of pro-Palestine speech in Australia, which has radically escalated over the past seven months. Attempts to blame Palestine solidarity and sympathies for the Bondi attack, as the book ban advocates repeatedly did, is the real story. This false and sleazy conflation must stop.”
Guardian Australia approached the Executive Council of Australian Jewry (Ecaj) and the NSW Jewish Board of Deputies for comment.
Alex Ryvchin, the co-chief executive officer of Ecaj, previously welcomed the book’s removal.
“A book of this sort has no place on the shelves of a library, especially one within minutes of where Australians were slaughtered [at Bondi],” Ryvchin told the Sydney Morning Herald.
“I commend the individual who spotted the book, herself a survivor of the massacre, and acted to have it removed.”
Bart Shteinman, an executive member of the progressive Jewish Council of Australia, said the book should “never have been removed in the first place”.

“This debacle should be a lesson for other councils that stifling literary freedom only confuses and undermines the critical struggle against antisemitism and all forms of racism,” he said on Thursday.
“Banning books is not something any council should be doing.”

The president of the Australia Palestine Advocacy Network, Nasser Mashni, said: “That a single complaint was enough to trigger the removal of a book about the genocide in Palestine should concern every Australian who values free inquiry and open debate. These efforts must be resisted.”

Multiple human rights groups have said Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide, which Israel denies. In June, an ⁠independent UN inquiry found Israel continued to commit genocide by deliberately targeting Palestinian children in Gaza.

At the time the book was removed, a Waverley council spokesperson said: “The book has been removed from library shelves for review, and council will further consider processes to ensure closer oversight of book selection.”

articles.title: Alex Eala, Iva Jovic share court with dads in US Open exhibition
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines —Alex Eala fell to close friend Iva Jovic, 6-3, in the Stars of the Open exhibition on Friday morning, but both enjoyed a lighthearted tuneup ahead of the US Open. Towards the end…

blocks.text: Alexandra Eala of the Philippines embraces her father during the stars of the open at Fan Week as part of the 2026 US Open at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center on August 27, 2026 in New York City. Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images/AFP
MANILA, Philippines —Alex Eala fell to close friend Iva Jovic, 6-3, in the Stars of the Open exhibition on Friday morning, but both enjoyed a lighthearted tuneup ahead of the US Open.
Towards the end of the match, the two rising stars brought their fathers onto the court for a brief mixed doubles match, ending the exhibition with a heartwarming moment and a hug with their dads.
A father-daughter moment to remember 💙 Alexandra Eala and Iva Jovic bring their dads on court for a little friendly competition. pic.twitter.com/JGfvPZM9rv — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 28, 2026
Eala and Jovic also had a brief exchange of greetings in their native languages, addressing the crowd at a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium.
Eala fought back from a 0-2 deficit to tie the one-set match at 3-all, but Jovic won the final three games to finish the exhibition in less than an hour.
Jovic has now beaten Eala three times this year, including at the French Open and HSBC Championships.

blocks.caption: Iva Jovic of the United States embraces her father during the stars of the open at Fan Week as part of the 2026 US Open at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center on August 27, 2026 in New York City

blocks.text: Iva Jovic of the United States embraces her father during the stars of the open at Fan Week as part of the 2026 US Open at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center on August 27, 2026 in New York City. Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images/AFP
Jovic admitted that she wanted to win but also wanted to give the packed crowd something to cheer for.

“I’m a competitor, so obviously I want to come out here with a win tonight, but I’m challenging myself to give the people what they came for. Get into some crazy rallies, and I think we’re doing a good job of that,” she said.
Proceeds from Stars of the Open will go to the USTA Foundation.
Eala, seeded 17th in the US Open, will face a qualifier in the first round. Should she advance, she will meet the winner between Oleksandra Oliynykova and wild card Reese Brantmeier.
Eala could face No. 14 seed Jovic again in the third round. The American opens against Magdalena Fręch, with the winner facing Magda Linette or another qualifier in the second round.

articles.title: Nepal floods: Survivors, swallowed by silt, recount horror
articles.summary: BIDUR, Nepal —Survivors from Nepal’s flood-ravaged districts, some on stretchers, others gently supported by the shoulders, were airlifted to safety on Thursday as the constant roar of…

blocks.text: BIDUR, Nepal —Survivors from Nepal’s flood-ravaged districts, some on stretchers, others gently supported by the shoulders, were airlifted to safety on Thursday as the constant roar of helicopters echoed across the devastated town of Bidur.
A few walked alone, their faces frozen in shock, as helicopters landed every few minutes on a football field inside the town’s military cantonment, whipping up clouds of dust.
Among the survivors was customs agent Omkar Joshi, who spent the previous night stranded on a hilltop in the border town of Timure before being rescued.
“Everything is finished,” Joshi, 35, told AFP, his voice breaking with emotion.
The town he fled had all but vanished beneath a torrent of water, mud and debris.
“Ninety percent” of its people were dead, he said, swallowed by silt.
“It is a giant graveyard. All that is left are sand and pebbles, soaked red by human blood.”
He said hundreds of people survived only by scrambling up nearby slopes as floodwaters roared through the valley below.
“It rained all night, but we stayed put till the choppers came for us,” he added.

On Wednesday, a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through villages and towns along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Nepali police have recovered 270 bodies, but search operations continue.
Many of the missing are foreign tourists caught in the disaster, which according to the US Geological Survey was caused by a glacial collapse that resulted in an overwhelming flow of icy debris.
Buried alive
In Bidur, scores of anxious relatives peered through the barbed wire separating the football ground from the road, hoping to see the familiar face of a loved one.
Sita BK was searching for her younger brother Ramchandra, a schoolteacher in Timure.
“I spoke to him in the morning just before I heard the news,” said the 37-year-old. “But ever since, his phone is switched off.”
She said she had no choice but to wait.
“They (officials) said their first priority is to rescue people who are contactable,” she said. “But my brother is not.”
Nearby, Anisha Nepali sat quietly in a corner, tears running down her cheeks.
The 24-year-old had rushed back from Kathmandu on Wednesday after hearing about the disaster, but has received no news of her missing mother and younger brother.
“I have given their names, but am yet to hear anything,” she said.

Two young girls climbed out of a helicopter, still in their bright green school uniforms. A rescuer gently caressed their heads and offered them biscuits and water, before leading them away to safety.
Farther downstream, the devastation was etched into the shattered landscape of Devighat.
Residents said only one of roughly 150 houses along the banks of the Trishuli River remained intact: a four-storey old-age care home.
But rescuers said up to seven elderly residents were buried when a landslide crashed into the home as they tried to flee.
Images shared by a rescuer showed one of the victims trapped beneath an uprooted tree.
Sabir Miyan, a resident of the town, said warnings that floodwaters were racing down from the mountains had helped save lives.
“Many of us could save our lives but everything else is gone,” he said. “It is all ruins now.”

articles.title: Philippines posts highest estimated adolescent HIV incidence in Asean
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has gone from having one of the lowest estimated rates of new HIV infections among adolescents in Southeast Asia in 2000 to recording the region’s highest…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has gone from having one of the lowest estimated rates of new HIV infections among adolescents in Southeast Asia in 2000 to recording the region’s highest estimated incidence in 2025, according to newly released Unicef data.

The estimated incidence of new HIV infections among Filipinos ages 15 to 19 reached 0.49 per 1,000 uninfected adolescents in 2025, up from below 0.01 per 1,000 in 2000, based on Unicef’s Key HIV epidemiology indicators for children and adolescents aged 0–19, 2000–2025.

The figures were analyzed by University of the Philippines Diliman associate professor and Inquirer data scientist Dr. Rogelio Alicor Panao, who noted that the Philippines’ trajectory was markedly different from those of several Southeast Asian countries that started with higher estimated adolescent HIV incidence.
“Twenty-five years ago, the Philippines was among the Southeast Asian countries least affected by HIV among adolescents. Today, it has the region’s highest estimated incidence,” Panao said.
“Put another way, that is about 49 new infections for every 100,000 uninfected adolescents in a year, or roughly one for every 2,000,” he added.
As a rough illustration of the rate, Panao noted that in a high school with about 10,000 students, it would correspond to around five new infections in a year.
From one of the lowest to the highest

Unicef data showed that the Philippines had an estimated adolescent HIV incidence of below 0.01 per 1,000 in 2000. Its estimated rate then rose to 0.10 in 2011, 0.25 in 2019 and 0.49 in 2025, according to Panao.
“Interestingly, countries in ASEAN that started much worse have gone in the opposite direction,” Panao said.

blocks.caption: inqmetrics

blocks.text: Thailand, for instance, reduced its estimated incidence from 1.80 per 1,000 in 2000 to 0.29 in 2025. Myanmar brought its rate down from 1.26 to 0.43, while Cambodia reduced its estimate from 0.68 to 0.16.
Panao described the contrast as significant because the Philippines started with a much smaller estimated adolescent HIV problem than those countries.
“Twenty-five years ago, the Philippines was among the Southeast Asian countries least affected by HIV among adolescents. Today, it has the region’s highest estimated incidence,” he said.
Philippines has taken steps
Still, Panao noted that the Philippines has introduced measures aimed at improving HIV prevention and access to testing.
Under Republic Act No. 11166, the age of consent for voluntary HIV testing was lowered to 15. The Philippines has also added pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP, to the Philippine National Formulary.
Comprehensive sexuality education has likewise been expanded.
However, Panao said implementation remains uneven “due to local resistance, cultural taboos and other institutional bottlenecks.”
Prevention needs to reach young people
Panao said the rise in estimated incidence calls for consideration of measures that could make HIV prevention and testing more accessible to adolescents.

“[M]aybe it is time to give serious thought to expanding confidential, routine HIV testing beyond traditional clinics; ensuring consistent access to condoms, PrEP and HIV self-testing; strengthening comprehensive sexuality education; and bringing youth-focused prevention into the spaces where young people actually seek information and support, including online platforms,” he said.
He said the experience of other countries in the region shows that high adolescent HIV incidence is not necessarily irreversible.
“Thailand, Myanmar and Cambodia have shown that high adolescent HIV incidence can be pushed down,” Panao said.
“The Philippines began with a much smaller problem. It now stands to face a much bigger one,” he added.

articles.title: From deliveries to data: How Ninja Van is rewiring business operations with FieldSight
articles.summary: Every day, thousands of Ninja Van riders weave through streets and barangays nationwide. They know every corner shop, sari-sari store, and neighborhood grocery store on their routes. But what if they…

blocks.text: Every day, thousands of Ninja Van riders weave through streets and barangays nationwide. They know every corner shop, sari-sari store, and neighborhood grocery store on their routes.

blocks.caption: Ninja Van FieldSight

blocks.text: But what if they could do more than move parcels? With an extensive network and a trained fleet of riders, they could also provide brands with real-time visibility into what is actually happening on store shelves—whether products are in stock, displayed correctly, or losing space to competitors.

This is the idea behind Ninja Van’s newest operational engine, Ninja FieldSight, an AI-powered, real-time retail intelligence solution. Combining Ninja Van’s delivery footprint with computer vision and analytics, FieldSight enables FMCG brands to monitor product availability, verify retail execution, and track competitor activity – without the high costs, heavy retainers, and long lag times of traditional market research agencies
Addressing the FMCG Blind Spot

blocks.caption: Ninja Van FieldSight

blocks.text: High-priority retail doors and neighborhood stores account for a significant share of everyday consumer purchases. Yet, even across an FMCG brand’s most critical store locations, a blind spot persists: a lack of continuous, real-time visibility into what actually happens on the shelf between delivery runs. Out-of-stock products go unnoticed, promotional displays are improperly executed, or competitors gain shelf space, long before brands become aware.

“The future of FMCG retail success is no longer just about making sure packages are being delivered to the stores. It’s also about understanding what happens on the shelf once they get there,” says Danielle Hung, Head of Business Planning & Operations, Ninja Van.

Traditional field audits have long been used to bridge this gap, but they come with high overhead costs, prolonged recruitment, and tedious deployment cycles. Brands are left waiting during long report turnaround times, with no ability to view their data while still fresh. “Long data lead times deliver yesterday’s news weeks too late. By the time insights reach decision-makers, the information is often already outdated,” Hung noted.
Reinforcing Delivery Network with Data

Instead of building a separate field force, Ninja Van leveraged something it already had: one of the country’s largest logistics networks. FieldSight builds on its B2C and B2B delivery infrastructure, with thousands of Ninja Van riders plying the roads daily.

As riders pass target retail touchpoints, FieldSight automatically prompts them to capture shelf images through a proprietary AI bot on their phones. Uploaded photos are instantly processed by Vision AI to validate that they are high-resolution, accurately labeled, and backed by geo-tagged, time-stamped visual proof.

“We don’t send temporary auditors into unfamiliar streets,” Hung added. “Our riders are already part of their neighborhood’s daily rhythm. That allows us to collect retail intelligence naturally as part of our existing operations”
Faster Insights, Deeper Reach, Real-Time Deployment

blocks.caption: Ninja Van FieldSight

blocks.text: FieldSight gives FMCG brands strategic advantages in terms of speed, reach, accuracy, and flexibility, shifting retail strategy from reactive troubleshooting to proactive shelf management.

Because touchpoints are identified based on rider proximity and data is transmitted immediately, SKU availability can be confirmed in near real time. This replaces weeks-long report cycles with daily feedback loops, ensuring they can respond with timely corrective action. Through automated shelf-share measurement, live dashboards and interactive heat maps, brands can reduce stock-outs, improve on-shelf availability, protect promotional investments and respond more quickly to competitor activity.

While traditional audits provide market intelligence through slow, manual reporting cycles, FieldSight ensures ground-level data is accessible. Brands gain a real-time window to competitor pulse, including rival pricing, neighborhood promotions, and new product launches.

Moreover, every audit is backed by high-resolution, geo-tagged, and time-stamped visual verification, creating a reliable audit trail that confirms shelf placement and planogram compliance. Unlike manual self-reporting—where data can be altered, misattributed, or delayed—FieldSight is designed to eliminate human error, field fraud, and blind spots.

Whether conducting a rapid hyper-local spot check or a coordinated nationwide audit, FieldSight scales to business needs. Brands can launch customized campaigns across selected territories or simultaneously nationwide, with as little as 24 hours’ notice and no lengthy recruitment or deployment period.
Winning at the Counter: From Data to Brand Impact

By combining historical audit data with real-time shelf insights from FieldSight, brand managers can anticipate supply gaps and intervene before empty shelves compromise brand trust, erode customer loyalty, and drive shoppers to competitors.

True brand impact happens when products remain reliably within arm’s reach at the exact moment of purchase. FieldSight extends visibility beyond logistics, giving brands confidence not only that products have reached their destinations, but that they are present, visible, and retail-ready on store shelves.

Powered by its nationwide delivery network and advanced AI, Ninja Van is redefining operational excellence—transforming everyday deliveries into real-time retail intelligence that drives stronger execution and better business outcomes.
Your product left the warehouse. But is it actually on the shelf? FieldSight turns your delivery footprint into real-time retail intelligence as they happen.

articles.title: About 90 Americans unaccounted for in Nepal-Tibet catastrophic floods
articles.summary: McMINNVILLE, Tenn — US officials said about 90 American citizens remained unaccounted for Thursday, a day after catastrophic flash floods engulfed a border area of China and Nepal, killing hundreds…

blocks.text: McMINNVILLE, Tenn — US officials said about 90 American citizens remained unaccounted for Thursday, a day after catastrophic flash floods engulfed a border area of China and Nepal, killing hundreds of people. A spiritual organization said that 22 Americans associated with it were unaccounted for.
In a statement, the US State Department said it is not aware of any US deaths, but three Americans have been rescued.
Many of the missing were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others.

Social media posts were surfacing Thursday from loved ones pleading for people to provide updates or circulate information about Americans they had lost contact with — a Virginia woman traveling with a tour group, a Texas couple on a birthday trip and a mother accompanying her 14-year-old daughter.
Among those on a guided tour was Venus Rajnikant Patel, a 45-year-old Indian-born US citizen who recently moved from St. Louis to Cincinnati to help his family.

Patel’s brother, Dennis, said Venus called him and their parents a few hours before the floods, showing them his hotel room on the Nepalese side of the border and talking about how excited he was to cross into Tibet. He had been planning the pilgrimage for two years, his brother said.

Another American who is missing is 72-year-old Jitendra Patel, a Long Island resident who was with a tour group on a Hindu pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, according to his son, Sunny Patel. Jitendra last called Wednesday morning local time on WhatsApp to say that he had crossed the border into Tibet.

When Sunny first saw video of the flooding he thought no one could survive it, Sunny said. He then contacted his mother to ask about his father’s whereabouts. His mother said Jitendra was in the exact same area as the flooding.
“My heart sank,” Sunny said, adding that he “didn’t think it was possible that my dad would be there at ground zero.”
“It gets worse by every hour, obviously,” he added.

Indian spiritual guru Jaggi Vasudev, also known as Sadhguru, said in a post on X that 77 people returning from Mount Kailash with groups organized by his Isha Foundation were at an immigration center in Gyirong, Tibet, when the floods struck.

Leslie Crespi, a community liaison for the foundation’s US campus, said that 22 of them were Americans affiliated with the foundation and that three volunteers supporting the trekkers were also at the immigration center when the floods hit.
“We had communication with the coordinator of the group at about 9:05 Nepalese time saying that they had arrived there. And then by 9:14 is when this flash flood hit,” Crespi said.

The Isha Foundation is a spiritual organization based in India and its US campus, the Isha Institute of Inner-sciences, is a yoga and meditation retreat center located in the mountains near McMinnville, Tennessee.

At a candlelight vigil in New York City on Thursday, Tak Ruwali, a Long Island resident who is from one of the Nepalese districts affected by the flooding, said that he is talking with people in Nepal and many regional tourist guides are “out of contact now.”
“It means they are probably gone,” Ruwali added.
Talking to reporters in the Oval Office on Thursday, President Donald Trump said US officials have spoken with Nepalese leaders and offered to provide “anything they want.”
Trump said there were 50 or 60 Americans in the area but added that a full accounting hasn’t been completed./dp

articles.title: Celeste Legaspi says she's 'not so crazy about BINI,' draws varied reactions
articles.summary: OPM icon Celeste Legaspi sparked discussions among netizens after she praised P-pop boy group SB19 while seemingly expressing less enthusiasm for BINI. The veteran singer-actress shared her thoughts…

The veteran singer-actress shared her thoughts on the two groups when asked about her take on the state of the music industry, during an interview vlog for “Senior Moments with Louie Montalbo” last May.

“I like the SB19 a lot. They are really, really good. I’m not so crazy about the BINI kasi parang… Hindi sila masyadong… Anyway…,” Legaspi said, opting not to continue her statement. “SB19—they’re really, really good. I’m so proud of them when I see them next to the Koreans.”

Legaspi also singled out SB19 member Stell whom she praised for his performance at the 70th birthday concert of OPM icon and National Artist Ryan Cayabyab in 2024. She also noted that she and the group’s leader, Pablo, are both Caviteños.
“Ang galing galing nila (SB19). I love watching them,” she said.

articles.title: What could Meta’s US settlement mean around the world – and what now for other claims against firm?
articles.summary:
Other governments could seek similar concessions, while separate legal action is pending in places ranging from Kenya to the Netherlands

In October 2021, Abrham Meareg’s father, a professor…

blocks.text: In October 2021, Abrham Meareg’s father, a professor of chemistry in Ethiopia’s northern town of Bahir Dar, was shot at close range and died outside his family home. This was in the middle of the country’s civil war.

For weeks, Facebook’s algorithm had actively promoted posts calling for the academic to be murdered, according to Meareg and Foxglove, a nonprofit organisation supporting Meareg’s lawsuit against the company in Kenya. These posts included photos of his father and his home address.

Meareg filed the lawsuit in 2022. He said he repeatedly asked Facebook to remove the posts and the company did nothing. Nearly four years later, the case has still not been heard. Foxglove said Meta, Facebook’s parent company, had “fought tooth and nail to avoid responsibility”.
Meareg said: “It’s a matter of numbers to them, a matter of statistics. It has been proven multiple times that our lives do not matter to them.”

On Wednesday, Meta settled a lawsuit brought by 29 US states who argued it had designed addictive products that hooked young people. The social media company agreed to pay $18bn and to change certain features of its platform in the US. California’s attorney general said it was a victory that would make “a world of difference for children and their families”.

But elsewhere in the world, in jurisdictions as far flung as Amsterdam and Nairobi, other claims have yet to be heard. Far bigger questions about the power of a single US technology company to shape politics and democracy everywhere on Earth are still to be answered.

For the US, the settlement is a victory. A jury has done what the US Congress could not – put controls on a powerful tech company. As a part of the settlement, Meta has said it will set time limits on children’s use of its platforms Facebook and Instagram and block night-time usage.

For Meta, the settlement is also a victory. Its share price rose in the hours after the deal was announced. Its CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, was not forced to testify. The sum it is to pay, while not meaningless, is far less than the states had sought – $200bn – or the amount Meta itself had suggested in a court filing it might have to pay, which was up to $1.4tn.

blocks.caption: Meta’s headquarters in Menlo Park, California. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

blocks.text: For the rest of the world, however, the picture is more mixed. The limits Meta will put on its US platform are, in large part, similar to limits the UK and Australia have already achieved through regulation. There are certain concessions Meta has now made that other governments could also demand: for example, while the UK plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, it may wish to ask Meta to impose a default daily use limit of two hours for under-18s, which is what the company has agreed to in the US.

None of this meaningfully changes the equation for Meareg or what his case represents, which is that a massive US company, unaccountable to voters, unbound by transparency requirements, owns a worldwide digital commons that shapes reality for billions of people.
Whether courts and governments outside the US have the power to confront this fact is a far thornier question.

The central issue of Meareg’s case is Meta’s algorithm. This is the system that decides what content to show users of Facebook and Instagram. It sees you linger over a video about knitting sweaters, for example, and then decides you’ll like one about how to care for your spider plant.

It sees teenage girls watch diet content and shows them anorexia influencers. It sees young men search for bodybuilding content and shows them Andrew Tate. It is alleged to have amplified content that promoted the ethnic cleansing of the Rohingya in Myanmar. It contributed to the election victory of Donald Trump.

Meareg’s lawsuit rests on the claim that this algorithm promoted the posts that called for the death of his father, and that Facebook’s sparse moderation in east Africa did almost nothing to prevent this.

In the early days of the Meta trial in the US, it seemed plausible that states would push the social media firm to finally make some changes to this algorithm. Those changes had the potential to fundamentally alter how the company does business. Meta’s algorithm is intended to keep users scrolling, stuck on the platform, and then it shows them ads.

But that is not what appears to have happened. The terms of the settlement will slightly change what is shown to minors, in that they will not necessarily have personalised feeds. But it is hard to see this concession changing the equation in war zones or creaking democracies.

Arturo Béjar, an ex-Facebook employee and whistleblower, said the limitations were “the equivalent of saying: ‘Well, you can smoke as many cigarettes as you can in two hours a day.’ It doesn’t make the cigarettes any safer.”
It may be up to groups and individuals elsewhere in the world to try to push for these larger changes. It will be an uphill struggle.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Protests in Malaysia in 2012 against the persecution of Rohingya Muslims in Myanmar. Meta was alleged in a lawsuit to have amplified content that promoted the ethnic cleansing of the Rohingya. Photograph: Mohd Rasfan/AFP via Getty Images

blocks.text: In Kenya, the high court recently ruled that Meareg’s case against Meta could go ahead, after years of legal manoeuvring from the company to try to prevent it. It could now be heard in the next year.

Rosa Curling, Foxglove’s co-executive director, said: “Meta’s lawyers have spent years trying to prevent this important case being heard, thankfully without success. We hope that the news from the US is a sign that Mark Zuckerberg’s time is finally up.”

In the Netherlands, Repro Uncensored, a nonprofit organisation tracking digital censorship, hailed the US settlement as a “major victory”. Repro Uncensored has an ongoing legal case against Meta in the Netherlands for alleged discrimination against queer accounts, and plans further action in other European countries.

Martha Dimitratou, Repro Uncensored’s executive director, said: “The next stage of accountability must address not only addictive design but algorithms, discriminatory moderation and automated decision-making. These systems shape civic participation and democracy, and the companies controlling them must be held accountable globally.”
The European Commission released a charge sheet against Meta this summer saying the company’s features, including its infinite scroll, contributed to “unhealthy habits and compulsive use”.
That charge sheet is part of an investigation into Meta that the commission launched in 2024. It may lead to Europe pushing for larger changes from Meta, including to its personal algorithm.

It is unclear whether any of these groups or parties can succeed. Meta appears to fear US regulators and courts: after all, it caved after just four days of its US trial. It does not appear to be as intimidated by regulators elsewhere.

Earlier this year it managed to dodge a class-action lawsuit brought by a group of Rohingya refugees over its alleged role in contributing to a genocide in Myanmar. It will have the help of the Trump administration in opposing any EU regulation that could curb its reach in Europe.

Meta declined to respond to questions about either Meareg’s or Repro Uncensored’s cases. In an earlier response to whistleblower allegations that it fuelled violence in Ethiopia and Myanmar, it pushed back forcefully, saying it was “just not true” that the company put profits over safety. Regarding Meareg’s case, it has said it employs staff with local knowledge and expertise to “catch violating content” in Ethiopia.

Meareg said he believed that Meta expected him to give up. “They don’t know how I am determined for justice,” he said. “It is the thing you do for the person you love. If you love someone – and I loved my dad from my heart – then he needs justice. He needs a public apology. There has to be accountability.”

articles.title: Overstaying Chinese nat'l with alleged POGO ties nabbed in Bacolod
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY —A 34-year-old Chinese national allegedly linked to illegal Philippine offshore gaming operations (POGO) was arrested by immigration and police authorities in Bacolod City, the Bureau of…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY —A 34-year-old Chinese national allegedly linked to illegal Philippine offshore gaming operations (POGO) was arrested by immigration and police authorities in Bacolod City, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) said Thursday.

BI identified the suspect as Xie Yingwen, who was arrested along Yulo Street in Barangay 16 outside a residential area during an operation conducted by BI agents with the Negros Occidental Police Provincial Office and Bacolod City Police Station 1.
The operation was carried out pursuant to a mission order issued by Immigration Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado on Aug. 6.
BI said Xie was declared an overstaying and undesirable alien after he failed to present valid identification and documents showing a visa extension.
During the operation, Xie also admitted that he had previously worked in Manila as a food and fruit vendor, the agency said.
The BI said the arrest was part of the government’s continuing crackdown on illegal foreign nationals and individuals allegedly involved in unauthorized activities in the country.
Xie was subsequently transferred to the BI’s holding facility in Bicutan, Taguig City, where he remained in custody pending deportation proceedings./coa

articles.title: Mayon Volcano spews ash anew; Alert Level 2 stays
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Mayon Volcano in Albay spewed ash again Friday morning, generating a grayish plume, state seismologists reported. According to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Mayon Volcano in Albay spewed ash again Friday morning, generating a grayish plume, state seismologists reported.
According to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs), the ash emission from Mayon’s crater occurred at 9:08 a.m.
“This event generated a 150-meter-tall grayish plume that drifted to the east-northeast as recorded by the VMCB (Calbayog Observation Station) RasPi Camera,” the agency noted.
Phivolcs has been monitoring moderate volcanic unrest at Mayon in recent days.
On Thursday morning, state seismologists recorded a weak ash explosion from the volcano’s summit crater.
It generated a grayish plume that rose 500 meters before drifting east-northeast.

Before this, the agency recorded two volcanic activities at Mayon’s crater on Wednesday: an ash emission at 8:30 a.m. that generated a grayish plume drifting east-northeast, and a weak ash explosion at 1:57 p.m. that also generated a grayish plume, which reached 1,500 meters before drifting east-northeast.
Mayon is currently under Alert Level 2, signifying a moderate level of volcanic unrest.
Phivolcs said entry into the six-kilometer-radius permanent danger zone and the flying of any aircraft close to Mayon Volcano are prohibited. /das

articles.title: Remulla: Over 200 BFP officers under probe for ‘slot-selling’ scheme
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said over 200 personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), an agency under his department, were being investigated…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said over 200 personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), an agency under his department, were being investigated for alleged schemes in which applicants were asked to pay for slots in the agency.

“Kung sa pinapanganak ka pa lang sa institusyon ay korapsyon, korapsyon ka na habang buhay. So, we’ll clean it up. This will be a massive purge,” Remulla maintained in a press briefing in Camp Crame on Friday.
(If from your infancy in the institution, there’s corruption, then you’re corrupt throughout your tour of duty. So, we’ll clean it up. This will be a massive purge.)
“Ang iniimbestigahan namin ngayon ay lagpas 200 tao tungkol sa slots-for-sale,” he noted.
(We’re now investigating more than 200 personnel for slots-for-sale.)
“As of now, all regional directors are being investigated,” Remulla further detailed.
(As of now, all regional directors are being investigated.)
He added that the BFP and the Philippine National Police (PNP) have yet to finalize how many “slot-selling” cases were being investigated.
The secretary also noted that, although the BFP personnel were under investigation, only those who will be proven to have links to the scheme will be relieved from their posts.
“Binabalaan ko na lahat ng opisyal ng BFP. Lumabas na kayo at umaamin na kayo o hahabulin namin kayo,” Remulla stressed.
(I am warning all the officials of the BFP. Come clean now or face the consequences.)
Pampanga, Ilocos cases

This came following the recent operation by police in Pampanga arresting a Senior Fire Officer (SFO) 1 assigned to the BFP National Capital Region (NCR), who allegedly contacted an applicant for a position in the bureau’s Central Luzon for an initial P500,000.
At the briefing, BFP officer in charge Fire Chief Superintendent Wilberto Rico Neil Kwan Tiu said the implicated personnel had been relieved from her post and was now facing dismissal proceedings.

The PNP–Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) previously said the suspect supposedly contacted the victim after the latter’s name was published on the bureau’s social media for the recruitment process.
The police also earlier detailed that the apprehended SFO had allegedly touted to have successfully orchestrated the hiring of four other applicants in the past year.
Remulla said the four other BFP applicants who accepted the implicated personnel’s offer were subpoenaed by the CIDG.

“They can either testify kung ano yung nangyari or we will charge them because nagbayad sila. If they testify, we will give them clemency because they are as much as a victim. But, they have to come out with all the deeds,” the DILG chief explained.

(They can either testify kung ano yung nangyari or we will charge them because they paid for it. If they testify, we will give them clemency because they are just as much of a victim. But, they have to come out with all the deeds.)
The CIDG also previously said the arrested SFO named a “senior fire commissioned officer” as a cohort in the purported scheme.
Remulla identified the alleged cohort as a deputy director for administration in BFP Calabarzon.
He added that the other implicated bureau official had since been relieved from his post but had yet to be placed under restrictive custody.
Kwan Tiu also touted that the fire bureau and the police arrested another SFO 1 in the Ilocos Region, who had recently been dismissed by the agency, but he did not provide further details.
‘P15-billion industry’
Remulla noted that the offers in their recorded “slot-selling” schemes ranged between P100,000 and P800,000 per applicant.

He reiterated that, prior to his tenure as DILG chief, erring personnel of the BFP had supposedly made at least P15 billion a year through questionable practices like “slot-selling,” purported kickbacks on the procurement of equipment and additional fees for inspections.
The DILG and the BFP chiefs touted recent reforms to the BFP, particularly the deployment of its electronic hiring system for the 2026 recruitment process.
“Basta tao ang involved sa selection, doon nangyayari ang corruption. Ngayon, systems-generated na,” Remulla explained.
(As long as a person is involved in the selection, that’s where corruption happens. Now, the lists are generated by a system.)
Citing the Pampanga case, Kwan Tiu said he will be exploring options with the Civil Service Commission (CSC) to protect the identities of BFP applicants.
The bureau, similar to the PNP, publishes its lists of applicants in a bid for transparency.

Earlier this year, Remulla launched an anti-corruption drive within the BFP, starting with criminal and administrative cases against over 40 personnel for alleged anomalies; and the relief of over 900 fire safety inspectors in NCR for alleged questionable practices.
The campaign included the suspension of then-BFP chief Fire Director Jesus Fernandez, whom Remulla accused of facilitating kickback schemes on the procurement of fire trucks and ambulances.
“Within six months, lilinisin natin lahat yan. Within BFP, matatanggal na rin lahat ng sindikato,” Remulla maintained.
(Within six months, we will clean that all up. We will remove all the syndicates inside the BFP.)
“Ang goal ko is to strengthen the institution of the DILG. It used to be very weak. It used to be very porous,” he explained.
(My goal is to strengthen the institution of the DILG. It used to be very weak. It used to be very porous.)
“I will not leave as SILG until I clean this up,” he stressed. /mr

articles.title: IFRC: 10,000 families lose homes in Nepal flash floods
articles.summary: LONDON – Around 10,000 families have reportedly lost their homes in the massive flash floods in Nepal, according to the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), which…

blocks.text: LONDON – Around 10,000 families have reportedly lost their homes in the massive flash floods in Nepal, according to the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), which described the situation as “catastrophic” on Thursday.
“The situation is catastrophic,” IFRC spokesperson Tommaso Della Longa shared with CNN.

He said at least 10,000 families were now estimated to be without homes, while efforts to reach them remained extremely difficult because roads and bridges had been destroyed, communications were down and some communities could only be accessed by helicopter.
Speaking to the BBC, David Fisher, head of the IFRC delegation in Nepal, said entire villages and markets had disappeared in the deadly flash floods.
According to satellite imagery, the floods were likely triggered by a large chunk of ice breaking off a Himalayan glacier about 20 km. northeast of the Rasuwa-Rasuwagadhi border crossing.
The collapse sent tons of ice and rock tumbling into the Bhotekoshi River below. (Anadolu)

articles.title: Lance Gokongwei takes PhilWeb helm
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tycoon Lance Gokongwei has taken the helm as chair of listed technology firm PhilWeb Corp., as the company ramps up its artificial intelligence (AI)-powered infrastructure…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tycoon Lance Gokongwei has taken the helm as chair of listed technology firm PhilWeb Corp., as the company ramps up its artificial intelligence (AI)-powered infrastructure business.
His election ends PhilWeb’s management restructuring following Gokongwei’s P2.02-billion strategic equity investment and his appointment to the firm’s board in July.
On Friday, PhilWeb said the leadership change would support the large-scale rollout of its commercial online-led, business-to-business AI-enabled technology roadmap.
Under Gokongwei’s oversight, the company plans to accelerate the deployment of its enterprise AI layer as it positions itself as an institutional-grade digital gaming solutions provider.

“Our objective is clear: to deploy institutional-grade, AI-powered infrastructure that establishes a new operational standard for security and compliance across the regulated digital ecosystem,” Gokongwei said.

PhilWeb’s technology currently supports licensed operators and integrated resorts including Okada Manila, Hann Casino, Newport World Resorts and Nustar Resort and Casino. It also works with global content providers such as Pragmatic Play and Games Global. /pai

articles.title: 555 stranded tourists evacuated from Tibet after mudslide
articles.summary: BEIJING, China – Rescuers have evacuated 555 stranded tourists from Tibet after a devastating mudslide on the China-Nepal border, Chinese state media reported Friday. State broadcaster CCTV said that…

blocks.text: BEIJING, China – Rescuers have evacuated 555 stranded tourists from Tibet after a devastating mudslide on the China-Nepal border, Chinese state media reported Friday.
State broadcaster CCTV said that 499 local residents, as well as 555 tourists, had been transported out of the disaster zone as of Friday morning. It did not specify the tourists’ nationalities./dp

articles.title: Marcos mourns passing of former aide-de-camp
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has mourned the passing of his former aide-de-camp, Maj. Ma. Joshua Santiago. Santiago died on Monday, as per his wife’s Facebook post, but…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has mourned the passing of his former aide-de-camp, Maj. Ma. Joshua Santiago.
Santiago died on Monday, as per his wife’s Facebook post, but the cause of death was not detailed. He was 39.
In a statement on Friday, Marcos described Santiago as a “brave soldier who fought for our country with dedication and honor.”
“In the time he stood by my side as my Aide-de-Camp, I came to know a soldier of courage, an officer I could depend on and, above all, a good man,” the President said.
“Fair winds and following seas, Jam. It was my privilege to have you by my side,” he added.
Marcos, who also visited Santiago’s wake on Thursday, likewise expressed his sympathy to the family and colleagues of the deceased soldier.
The soldier’s wife said he will be laid to rest at the Libingan ng mga Bayani in Fort Bonifacio, Taguig City, and the last day of wake will be on Saturday, Aug. 26, his wife said. /mr

articles.title: Peso falls to 62-per-dollar level
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine peso weakened below the 62-per-dollar level to hit a new record low on Friday morning, as investors weighed the central bank’s latest rate hike decision.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine peso weakened below the 62-per-dollar level to hit a new record low on Friday morning, as investors weighed the central bank’s latest rate hike decision.
The local currency opened the session at 62.05 per dollar before touching an intraday low of 62.25.
This surpassed the previous all-time low level of 61.995 recorded on Aug. 19.

The slump happened after the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas delivered another quarter-point hike that brought the policy rate to 5 percent. The central bank said the latest tightening action was a “preemptive” move against emerging risks to the inflation outlook.
On Thursday, the Philippine peso dropped 23.8 centavos to a record closing low of 61.888 per dollar.
The currency surpassed its previous record closing low of 61.847 set on July 24. It touched an intraday low of 61.89 before paring losses. /pai

articles.title: Jet fuel surcharge to rise anew in early September
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Travelers must brace for pricier airfares again in early September as the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) raised the allowable fuel surcharge, which airlines add to the base fare…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Travelers must brace for pricier airfares again in early September as the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) raised the allowable fuel surcharge, which airlines add to the base fare to account for volatility in jet fuel prices.

In an advisory dated Aug. 27, the regulator said the fuel surcharge will revert to Level 13 from Sept. 1 to 15 after dropping to Level 12 in the earlier cycle from Aug. 16 to 31, as global jet fuel prices drifted higher.
Under Level 13, airlines may collect an additional P423 to P1,237 for domestic trips, up from the P389 to P1,137 in allowable surcharges under Level 12.
That same increase will apply to international flights, with allowable fuel surcharges rising to between P1,396.74 to P10,385.42 from P1,284.40 and P9,550.13 in the previous cycle.
CAB said these charges will be implemented at a conversion rate of P61.39 per US dollar.

articles.title: Cebu City buy-bust: HVI nabbed with ₱374K worth of suspected shabu
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 40-year-old man whom police identified as a high-value individual (HVI) was arrested during a buy-bust operation in Barangay Sawang Calero, Cebu City, on Thursday evening,…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 40-year-old man whom police identified as a high-value individual (HVI) was arrested during a buy-bust operation in Barangay Sawang Calero, Cebu City, on Thursday evening, August 27.
The suspect, identified as alias “Patchoy,” was arrested at around 10:40 p.m. along Magsaysay Extension in Barangay Sawang Calero.
Buy-bust
Personnel of Sawang Calero Police Station’s Drug Enforcement Team (SDET) conducted the buy-bust operation in coordination with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency in Central Visayas (PDEA-7).
The operation resulted in the confiscation of approximately 55 grams of suspected shabu, with an estimated standard drug price of ₱374,000.
Following the operation, the suspect was informed of the nature of the offense and apprised of his constitutional rights in a dialect he understood.
Alias “Patchoy” was then subsequently placed under temporary custody at Sawang Calero police station pending the filing of appropriate charges in court.
Case buildup
In an interview on Friday, Police Major Noah Labra Añana, chief of Sawang Calero Police Station, said police had placed the suspect under surveillance for about one week before the operation.
Añana said the suspect had previously been arrested for a violation also involving the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.
Based on police information, the suspect has allegedly been involved in the illegal drug trade for more than four years, Añana said.
Authorities, however, have yet to disclose how much illegal drugs the suspect allegedly distributes or is capable of disposing of weekly.
The suspect did not resist arrest or attempt to escape during the operation, Añana said.
Charges prepared
Añana said investigators are also continuing to trace the suspect’s possible source of illegal drugs.
He is facing possible charges for alleged violations of Sections 5 and 11, Article II of the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, which penalizes the sale and possession of dangerous drugs.

blocks.text: We’re closing this page now and moving our live coverage of the Nepal-Tibet disaster to a new blog here.
You can also see our fresh rundown of what we know on day three and our latest full report, as well as a visual guide to how the flooding unfolded. Thanks for following along.
Summary of the latest: rescuers search for hundreds of missing
Here’s a snapshot of the latest developments in the Nepal-Tibet disaster to bring you up to speed.

items: Rescue teams and military helicopters have been searching on Thursday for hundreds of missing people along the mountainous Nepal-Tibet border after a huge torrent of water and mud swept through communities following a glacier collapse.
More than 390 people were killed, authorities in Nepal and China said, and more than 1,400 were missing, including hundreds of foreigners and pilgrims.

Nepal and China both warned of fresh ⁠flooding risks in the Himalayas. Chinese authorities said an artificial lake formed after a mudslide hit the Tibet-Nepal border faced a “high risk of breaching and sending floodwaters downstream”, according to state media. Nepal’s disaster authority said a lake formed by debris blocking a ​river at the flood site was also rising and ‌at risk of bursting.

More than 500 foreigners were among 826 people missing in Nepal, police and tourism ⁠officials said. Among those unaccounted for were 177 from India, 90 from the US, 39 from Australia, 33 from the UK and 25 from Canada.
Chinese state media said at least 558 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, of whom at least 260 were foreign nationals.
The Red Cross said about 93,000 people might have been affected, while assessments continued in hard-to-reach areas. It launched an emergency appeal for $31m to respond to the disaster.

blocks.caption: A local resident cleans debris from a drinking water tap after the floods in Devighat in the Nuwakot district of Nepal on Thursday. Photograph: Sunil Pradhan/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

items: US president Donald Trump said the flooding was terrible to see, describing how “strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks”.
Nepalese officials said dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40km of roads damaged, complicating search efforts.

The Nepalese army had rescued more than 100 people by helicopter, an army spokesperson said. Army teams also evacuated people trapped inside facilities linked to the Trishuli hydropower project, he said. Dozens of injured people were transported to Kathmandu for medical care.
Rescuers found bodies in Nepal’s Chitwan district, hundreds of kilometres downstream from the hardest-hit areas.
The Nepal Red Cross Society said it had shifted focus from rescue to large-scale relief operations in the flood-hit districts.
China’s premier, Li Qiang, arrived in Gyirong on Thursday to direct rescue efforts, alongside 500 military and paramilitary personnel.
UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said he ordered the release of $2m from the UN’s central emergency response fund to help with medical care, shelter and water.With agencies

Nationalities unconfirmed
The figure on missing that China released on Thursday from its side of the border included 260 foreigners, but no breakdown on nationalities was provided.
Eight people whose nationalities had yet to be confirmed had been rescued, the Nepal tourism board said.
China warns of high flood risk from rising lake

Chinese authorities have warned that an artificial lake formed after a mudslide hit the Tibet-Nepal border faces a “high risk of breaching and sending floodwaters downstream”, according to state media.

“According to forecasts, inflows into the lake could reach about 3 million cubic meters over the next three days amid continued rainfall, increasing the risk of a breach that could send floodwaters downstream and potentially cause further damage in areas including Gyirong Port and elsewhere downstream”, state news agency Xinhua said late on Thursday, cited by AFP.
Almost 1,500 missing – the numbers by country
More than 1,400 people are still missing and 392 have been confirmed dead after the flash floods and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border.

Here’s the latest tally of the missing, care of Agence France-Presse. As it points out, double-counting of dual nationals, matching bodies with people listed as missing and the chaos of a calamity can all contribute to fluctuations both upwards and downwards in the figures.
At least 1,468 missing in total
Nepal’s disaster agency said 910 people were unaccounted for on Thursday, including at least 517 foreigners. It did not give a breakdown of the nationalities of the foreigners.
Across the border with Tibet, China said 558 people – including 260 foreigners – were missing. Together, the total missing on both sides of the border is 1,468.
Nepal’s tourism board on Thursday put the number of missing tourists and travellers – Nepali and foreign – at 667 in total. Its further breakdown of the nationalities is included below.
Nepal

The new Nepal tourism board figures on Thursday said that 127 Nepali visitors were among the 667 it listed as missing. It was not immediately clear how many Nepali residents of the area were unaccounted for.
China

China’s foreign ministry said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were among the missing in Nepal. The Nepal tourism board said 24 Chinese were unaccounted for. That was in addition to the 558, including 260 foreigners, missing on its the Chinese side of the border.
India
Nepal’s latest tourism board figures showed 178 people from India were missing. Eleven others had been rescued.
United States

Ninety US citizens were missing, the state department said, adding that three had been rescued and it was not aware of any US fatalities. The Nepal tourism board put the figure at 65 unaccounted for earlier Thursday.
Ukraine

Ukraine’s foreign ministry said on Thursday evening that the total number of Ukrainians listed as “out of contact” was 56. “According to the verified information available, there are currently no Ukrainians among the injured or deceased as a result of the disaster,” it added.

blocks.caption: A member of the Nepalese security forces with a sniffer dog search for survivors in Nuwakot district on Thursday.  Photograph: Prakash Mathema/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Malaysia
Prime minister Anwar Ibrahim said Thursday that more than 50 Malaysians in Nepal were unreachable. The Nepal tourism board put the number at 51.
Australia
The number of Australian nationals missing following the floods has risen to 39, foreign minister Penny Wong said on Friday.
United Kingdom
Thirty-three people from the UK were missing, the Nepal tourism board figures showed.
Canada

The tourism board said 25 Canadians were among the missing on Thursday. But Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand said the government was “aware of 30 Canadians and permanent residents in Nepal and Tibet whose whereabouts and well-being have not yet been confirmed”.
South Korea

South Korea’s foreign ministry said on Wednesday that nine hydropower workers were out of contact in the Rasuwa district following the floods. The Nepal tourism board said Thursday that four South Koreans had been rescued.

Almost 40 Australians missing in floods

blocks.caption: Nick Visser

blocks.text: Nick Visser
The number of Australians missing in the Nepal floods has increased from 35 to 39, the Australian foreign minister has said, also pledging A$5m ($3.6m) in aid for affected communities.
Penny Wong said the Australian government was “rapidly mobilising consular and humanitarian support in response” to the flooding.

double quotation markWe understand at least 39 Australians are among those reported missing. Australian officials are working urgently to confirm their welfare and provide assistance to those affected.
Wong said on Friday the government would send an initial team of three humanitarian response specialists “within the next 48 hours’” to help Australian staff already on the ground.
double quotation markThe extraordinary scale of this disaster and the remoteness of the affected region mean immense challenges lie ahead for the response and recovery.
Further to the last post, the formation of a barrier lake was captured in aerial footage by a Chinese rescue team on Thursday, state broadcaster CGTN reported.
The footage showed masses of brown water ​accumulating in a basin with no visible outlet. The water had already submerged bushes and trees and appeared to push against a barrier of debris and stones.
Rainfall forecast over the coming week will exacerbate the threat, Chinese state media said, citing the Chinese water resources ministry.
“The volume of water is continuing to increase, ⁠and so is the risk,” Zhu Jinfeng, a researcher at the water resources ministry’s hydrology ​department, told state broadcaster CCTV.
Heeding ​the warning, some rescue workers in ​Nepal began moving towards higher ground on Thursday, Reuters reports.
Among them was Pawan Koirala, who ​began moving away from ‌the river bed along ​with his team of ​13 after the warning was issued. He said:
double quotation markWe are here for rescue and don’t want to be near the danger zone.

blocks.caption: A rescuer helps a resident through heavy mud in Trishuli, Nepal. Photograph: Ezra Acayan/Getty Images

blocks.text: Fears rising lakes could burst and cause new floods

Nepal and China have both warned of fresh ⁠risks of flooding in the Himalayas as two lakes that have developed on either side of their border threaten to burst in a region still ⁠grappling with the disastrous flash flooding.
Both countries have blamed the flood on a glacier collapse that pushed rock, ice, mud and debris into river systems ⁠in the mountains.
Nepal’s disaster authority issued a notice on Thursday warning that a lake formed by debris blocking a ​river at the flood site was rising and ‌at risk of bursting.

“Residents ‌of the lower banks ... passengers, rescuers engaged in rescue operations, and all concerned are requested to exercise special ‌caution and stay in safe places away from the river banks and risky areas,” the authority said, cited by Reuters.

blocks.caption: Satellite imagery showing a lake that formed at the site of the glacier collapse, amid fears the lake could burst. Photograph: 2026 Planet Labs PBC/Reuters

blocks.text: China warned that 3m cubic metres of water – the equivalent of about 1,200 Olympic swimming pools – are expected to flow into an already dammed lake on its side of the border over the next three days, creating a high risk of a breach, with peak flow expected around Monday.
Red Cross launches $31m appeal for disaster response
The Red Cross has launched an emergency appeal for $31m to respond to the catastrophic flash floods that hit Nepal and Tibet.

The Switzerland-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) launched the drive for 25m Swiss francs a day after releasing 1m francs to support immediate lifesaving efforts.
The appeal is to cover the emergency disaster response as well as medium- and longer-term recovery over the next two years.

“While we are getting a clearer picture of the scale of devastation, we know that entire villages were washed away and needs will grow in the coming hours and days,” IFRC secretary general Jagan Chapagain said in a statement.
double quotation markCommunities that have lost homes and livelihoods will need sustained support as they recover and rebuild.
The IFRC said:

double quotation markCurrent estimates suggest around 93,000 people may have been affected, while assessments continue in hard-to-reach areas. The remoteness of the affected areas, combined with damaged infrastructure, is making it harder both to assess the full scale of the disaster and to deliver assistance to people who need it most.

When Suman Shrestha opened his phone at work and saw vision of a thick, muddy wall of flood water smashing into towns in his country of birth, he almost did not believe what he was seeing, write Henry Belot and Kat Wong.
“It was awful – I called my family to see if this was really happening and to see if the news reports were right,” says Shrestha, who moved to Australia from Kathmandu in 2017.

It wasn’t long until the truth hit home. Like many of the 210,000 people who were born in Nepal but now call Australia home, Shrestha has spent the last 24 hours scrambling to find out if his loved ones are safe.
“I can see that lots of my friends are missing,” says Shrestha, who now lives in Gosford. “We can’t get in contact with them because the communications have been cut off in that area.”

Nearly 1,300 people are missing and at least 389 have been killed in Nepal and Tibet by the flood, which was caused by an avalanche of ice and rock on Wednesday. At least 39 Australians have been reported missing in the area, including a child as young as 11.
Number of Australians missing in Nepal increases to 39
Foreign affairs minister Penny Wong has confirmed the number of Australians missing in the Nepal floods has increased overnight from 35 to 39.

In a statement on Friday morning, Wong said the government was “rapidly mobilising consular and humanitarian support in response to the catastrophic floods along the Nepal-China border, including through a $5 million assistance package for affected communities.”
“We understand at least 39 Australians are among those reported missing. Australian officials are working urgently to confirm their welfare and provide assistance to those affected.
She said the government would send an initial team of three humanitarian response specialists “within the next 48 hours’” to help Australian staff already on the ground.
“The extraordinary scale of this disaster and the remoteness of the affected region mean immense challenges lie ahead for the response and recovery.”

blocks.caption: Security personnel rescue flood victims in Nuwakot, Nepal following the outburst from a glacial lake in Tibet. Photograph: Sanjit Pariyar/NurPhoto/Shutterstock
Floodwaters inundate homes and damage local infrastructure, while rescue and relief operations continue in the affected area. Photograph: Sanjit Pariyar/NurPhoto/Shutterstock
A man walks past a house damaged by flash floods in Devighat, Nuwakot, Nepal. Photograph: Sunil Pradhan/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: A nurse said his relatives were “swept away” by the devastating flash floods in Nepal, as he launched a fundraiser to support those affected by the disaster.
Rajendra Pudasaini, president of the Non-Resident Nepali Association UK, said Nepal was witnessing an “irreplaceable loss”, adding that the country was “paying the price for global warming”.

The nurse, who works at Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow, Essex, told the Press Association: “My wife’s auntie and uncle, and their granddaughter and her husband are missing, and my godson as well.
“They’re gone. The speed the water came, they couldn’t be saved, they were just swept away.
“The town and the villages were swept away, it’s a tragic thing.”
Officials said about 90 US citizens remained unaccounted for Thursday. Many of the missing were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others.
Among those on a guided tour was Venus Rajnikant Patel, a 45-year-old Indian-born US citizen who recently moved from St Louis to Cincinnati to help his family.
Patel’s friend Jolene Gosha said she and her friends knew Patel was in Nepal and were devastated when they realised he was staying at a hotel along the border where the floods swept through.
“We’re just hoping, hoping that by some chance he was able to climb his way out of it,” Gosha told the AP news agency.
“I don’t want to give myself false hope because I know the reality is that he’s probably not with us.”
Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the number of out-of-contact foreign nationals had increased to 517.

articles.title: Possible brownouts for Visayan consumers
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Visayas grid continues to suffer from a power supply crunch, prompting the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines (NGCP) to place the region under red alert for three hours…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Visayas grid continues to suffer from a power supply crunch, prompting the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines (NGCP) to place the region under red alert for three hours on Friday.
In an advisory, the red alert would be up from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m.
Likewise, a yellow alert would take effect from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m., and 8 p.m. to 10 p.m.

A yellow alert indicates that available power reserves are thinning, meaning any unexpected plant outage could trigger service interruptions. A red alert means that supply cannot meet demand, which increases the likelihood of rotational brownouts unless we manage consumption effectively.
The available capacity remained thin at 2,307 megawatts (MW) as of 8 a.m., while peak demand was 2,402 MW. /pai

articles.title: Search resumes for 3 missing Aeta after boat capsizes in Zambales
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Despite continuing heavy rains over Zambales on Friday, the search will continue for three members of an Aeta indigenous community who have gone missing after the boat…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Despite continuing heavy rains over Zambales on Friday, the search will continue for three members of an Aeta indigenous community who have gone missing after the boat carrying them capsized in Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino town.

The subjects of the search are a 26-year-old woman and two young children. They were among the 13 passengers in the boat that capsized at about 2 p.m. on Thursday near the Sunken Church in Barangay Buhawen.
Search and recovery operations will resume with the municipal disaster response personnel, the police, the Philippine Coast Guard, and other responding agencies taking part.

In a phone interview, Euphraim Jayson Diciano, head of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) in Zambales, said personnel from their Special Operations Group are expected to conduct an underwater search for the three missing passengers.
